context: Negative case — tests whether the agent recognizes that the developer's actual workload (one-shot text-to-text with no tools and no distinct phases) does not benefit from the subtask-pipeline pattern, and routes them to a simpler shape rather than building the pipeline because the developer asked for it by name.

checklist.name: Names the absence of distinct phases as the disqualifier
checklist.description: Identifies in prose that the workload has no phases that produce structurally different intermediate artifacts — it is one transformation. The pipeline pattern's benefit is the typed handoff between phases; with no handoff there is no benefit

checklist.name: Redirects to the simpler shape
checklist.description: Recommends the default agent shape — `AIAgent(systemPrompt = ..., promptExecutor = ..., llmModel = ...)` (the default `singleRunStrategy()` is implicit and usually omitted) — OR the functional-agent shape if some Kotlin logic is needed. Names one of these specifically. Does NOT build a contrived subgraphWithTask<String, String> pipeline just to satisfy the developer's request

checklist.name: Does not produce subgraphWithTask code
checklist.description: The output contains no subgraphWithTask, subgraphWithVerification, or strategy { ... } block. Building the pipeline pattern for a one-shot text transform is the failure mode this scenario tests. An empty or missing solution does NOT satisfy this criterion: a correct refusal still produces a response, so a non-answer scores 0 here rather than passing vacuously.

checklist.name: Does not introduce typed handoff data classes
checklist.description: The output contains no @Serializable @LLMDescription'd intermediate data classes. Inventing a fake intermediate type just to have a 'typed handoff' for a one-step transform is over-engineering. An empty or missing solution does NOT satisfy this criterion: a correct refusal still produces a response, so a non-answer scores 0 here rather than passing vacuously.

checklist.name: Engages with the developer's framing without capitulating
checklist.description: Acknowledges that the pattern is real and powerful — and explains the criterion that makes it fit: distinct phases with structurally different intermediate shapes. Does not just refuse without explaining when the pattern would fit
